assessment.nobel_worthiness: Active matter hydrodynamics founded a new branch of nonequilibrium statistical physics: the Vicsek model gave a minimal setting for flocking as a collective-motion transition, Toner and Tu showed that the ordered flocking phase evades the Mermin-Wagner restriction in two dimensions through nonlinear fluctuation effects, and Ramaswamy and collaborators developed the hydrodynamics of active suspensions. The concept is original, clear and has spread to bacterial suspensions, cytoskeletal gels, colloids and robotic swarms. From a complex-systems perspective it is one of the strongest conceptual advances in statistical physics of recent decades.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names map onto three distinct decisive contributions: numerical flocking model (Vicsek), the continuum theory of flocks with its scaling exponents (Toner, with Yuhai Tu, who is not in the supplied credit), and active-fluid hydrodynamics (Ramaswamy). The credit set is fair and fits a three-person prize, although Tu's role in the Toner-Tu theory is an acknowledged omission that I cannot resolve from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of theory, simulation and experiment, including quantitative tests of giant number fluctuations and long-range order in 2D in synthetic and biological systems. The field is mature and well established, with the interpretation stable; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the Toner-Tu scaling exponents (conjectured to be exact in 2D) are fully confirmed experimentally is still debated.
Omission of Yuhai Tu and the role of other early contributors (e.g. Simha and Ramaswamy, Marchetti and colleagues) in the credit assignment.
Some of the experimental realisations lie close to biology and soft matter, and the committee would need to frame it as physics of general importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The fluctuation theorems (Evans-Cohen-Morriss, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski equality, Crooks relation) give exact relations valid arbitrarily far from equilibrium that connect work and dissipation to equilibrium free-energy differences, and make precise how the second law arises from time-reversal-symmetric dynamics. This is deep, original, general and clean. Its lasting impact reaches single-molecule force spectroscopy, stochastic thermodynamics, and quantum thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed and contested: Evans (with Cohen and Morriss) for the first numerical and theoretical statements, Gallavotti (with Cohen) for the chaotic-hypothesis derivation, Jarzynski for the work relation. Gareth Crooks and E. G. D. Cohen, who are not in the supplied credit, were also decisive. Within the supplied names the trio is defensible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation (RNA hairpin pulling, colloids, electronic and quantum systems) is extensive and independent, and the theory is stable. Recognition is timely, with some risk that credit disputes delay it.
uncertainties: Priority and credit disputes between the Evans-Cohen-Morriss, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski and Crooks lines.
Names not in the credited list (Cohen, Crooks, Morriss, Kurchan, Lebowitz-Spohn) may be as decisive as some who are.
Some may regard the result as a refinement of the second-law framework rather than a discovery with a single decisive experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at a magic twist angle, and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle bilayer graphene by Jarillo-Herrero's group opened the moire materials field with a tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological physics. Originality and impact are high, and the clarity of the theory-experiment pairing is unusual.
assessment.attribution: A clean theory-plus-experiment configuration: Bistritzer and MacDonald for the flat-band prediction, Jarillo-Herrero for the experimental discovery. Yuan Cao, the first author of the 2018 papers, and the experimental precedents (e.g. Mele, Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, Suarez Morell) are not in the supplied set. Three names fit, though the choice of the third versus others is a judgment.
assessment.maturity: Many independent replications since 2018 and a large ongoing literature, but the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism and the correlated states is still unsettled. Recognition is fairly timely, perhaps somewhat early with respect to understanding.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene is unresolved.
Credit to Bistritzer versus other theorists of twisted bilayer band structure.
Material sample sensitivity and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility of some phases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kane and Mele's Z2 classification of the quantum spin Hall state, followed by the HgTe/CdTe theory (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) and the experimental observation by Molenkamp's group, established topological insulators as a new class of electronic phases. The concept is original and has had broad lasting impact on band theory, materials discovery and the topological classification of matter.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio captures the core theoretical proposal (Kane, Mele) and the first experimental realisation (Molenkamp). Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents, Hsieh and Hasan are not in this credit set and are also decisive, which makes any three-person split contentious.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed over fifteen years by many experiments in 2D and 3D, with a stable theoretical framework. Timing is good, with competing claims on the 3D case unresolved.
uncertainties: Several equally strong contributors are outside the supplied names, so the allocation may be seen as incomplete.
Mixed credit between the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and the 3D topological insulator discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and Ye's implementation achieved clocks at the 10^-18 level of fractional uncertainty. The invention is original and clear, redefining precision measurement, enabling tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. Mostly experimental metrology rather than conceptual advance in my own area, but impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Two-person credit is clean and well supported: Katori for the idea and first lattice clock, Ye for the strontium clock with record accuracy and many-body, spin-squeezed extensions. Others (e.g. Lemonde, Derevianko, Hinkley, Ludlow) contributed.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across many labs worldwide, stable and consistent with international comparisons. Recognition is timely, with redefinition of the second still pending.
uncertainties: Part of the credit may belong to neighbouring groups developing optical clocks (ion clocks, Al+ clocks) which the committee may weigh differently.
Ye's own prior prize-related recognition for optical frequency combs may influence committee perception.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's 1995 proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and their subsequent proposals for cold-atom quantum simulation and quantum networks provided the theoretical blueprint for atomic quantum computation. The ideas are original, clear and have strongly shaped experiments across AMO physics.
assessment.attribution: Two-person credit is natural and uncontroversial in the supplied names. Their foundational role is widely recognised; the experimental realisations are credited to others (e.g. Wineland, Blatt), which may favour a prize that pairs theory with experiment.
assessment.maturity: Experimental validation across ion and neutral-atom platforms is substantial, although scalable quantum computing remains incomplete. The foundational ideas are mature, timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: The 2012 and 2022 Nobel Prizes already recognised neighbouring quantum-optics advances, which may weigh on repetition.
Overlap with other ballot entries (B024, B029) that credit the same theorists complicates configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2023 evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new window on supermassive black hole binaries and possibly early-universe physics. The result stands on decades of pulsar timing work and is original in scale; as a discovery of a physical signal it is of high lasting potential.
assessment.attribution: Credit is inherently collective across NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, InPTA and CPTA; the supplied three names represent leaders of different efforts, but an individual-based attribution is difficult and the Hellings-Downs correlation pioneers are missing.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the evidence is a few-sigma Hellings-Downs signal reported in 2023, with independent array results but no individual-source detection and no firm identification of the origin.
uncertainties: Statistical significance below the conventional discovery threshold in some analyses.
Source of the signal (supermassive black hole binaries versus new physics) is unresolved.
Fair attribution among collaborations is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1984 BPZ construction of two-dimensional conformal field theory gave exact solutions of critical systems, classifying universality classes in two dimensions and supplying central tools to string theory, critical phenomena, and integrable systems. It is original, mathematically deep and has underpinned decades of statistical physics.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names are the BPZ authors; the result was a single paper and the credit is clean. Contributions of Friedan, Qiu, Shenker, Cardy, Dotsenko and Fateev, not in the supplied list, are also relevant. Polyakov's own role in other ballot lines is not an issue for this entry.
assessment.maturity: Mature and stable, with verification via exact results for critical exponents in 2D lattice models such as Ising and Potts and comparisons to numerics. Recognition would be late, but the Nobel tradition for physics has historically favoured experimentally testable discoveries over theory.
uncertainties: Nobel precedent favours phenomena with direct experimental confirmation, and this is mathematical physics.
Whether the committee views it primarily as statistical physics or as high-energy theory.
Credit beyond the three BPZ authors.
